description:
The Decentralized People’s Nursery scheme was launched by the Government of India in 2016. 

This initiative is part of the larger National Afforestation Programme. 

The scheme aims to promote the establishment of nurseries at the grassroots level. 

It focuses on enhancing the availability of quality planting material for afforestation and reforestation activities. 

The primary objective of the Decentralized People’s Nursery scheme is to empower local communities. 

It encourages them to participate actively in the management of forest resources. 

The scheme aims to create a sustainable source of income for rural households. 

It also seeks to improve the ecological balance by increasing forest cover. 

The target is to establish at least 1,000 decentralized nurseries across various states. 

Each nursery is expected to produce a minimum of 50,000 saplings annually. 

The saplings produced will primarily consist of indigenous species. 

This is crucial for maintaining biodiversity and ecological stability. 

The scheme also aims to provide training and capacity building for local communities. 

This includes knowledge about nursery management and sustainable practices. 

The benefits of the scheme extend to both environmental and economic aspects. 

Each participating household can earn an estimated income of ₹30,000 to ₹50,000 per annum. 

This income is generated from the sale of saplings and related activities. 

The scheme is particularly beneficial for marginalized communities. 

It provides them with an opportunity to engage in sustainable livelihoods. 

Eligibility criteria for the Decentralized People’s Nursery scheme include being a resident of the area. 

Participants must also belong to Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes. 

Other eligible groups include women self-help groups and local farmers. 

There are no specific age limits for participation. 

However, participants are encouraged to have some basic knowledge of agriculture or horticulture. 

The application process for the scheme involves several steps. 

Interested individuals or groups must submit an application to the local forest department. 

The application should include details about the proposed nursery location and management plan. 

Required documents include proof of identity and residence. 

Additionally, a letter of support from the local community or gram panchayat is necessary. 

Once the application is submitted, it undergoes a review process. 

The local forest department conducts an assessment of the proposed site. 

If approved, the department provides financial assistance and technical support. 

The financial assistance can range from ₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh per nursery. 

This funding is aimed at covering initial setup costs such as infrastructure and seedlings. 

The disbursement of funds typically occurs in two installments. 

The first installment is released upon approval of the nursery. 

The second installment is released after the successful establishment of the nursery. 

The timeline for establishing a nursery is generally set at six months. 

Participants are expected to start producing saplings within this period. 

The scheme also emphasizes regular monitoring and evaluation. 

Local forest officials are responsible for overseeing the progress of each nursery. 

They provide ongoing support and guidance to ensure sustainability. 

The implementing authority for the Decentralized People’s Nursery scheme is the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. 

The scheme is executed through state forest departments. 

Each state has its own designated officials to manage the implementation. 

Contact details for local forest departments can be found on state government websites. 

The scheme has seen positive outcomes in various states. 

States like Madhya Pradesh and Odisha have reported successful establishment of nurseries. 

These nurseries have contributed significantly to local economies. 

They have also played a vital role in enhancing forest cover. 

The Decentralized People’s Nursery scheme aligns with the broader goals of the National Mission for a Green India. 

This mission aims to increase forest and tree cover by 33 percent by 2022. 

The scheme also supports the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. 

Particularly those related to climate action and sustainable livelihoods. 

In terms of statistics, the scheme has led to the establishment of over 500 nurseries by 2023. 

These nurseries have collectively produced more than 25 million saplings. 

The impact on local biodiversity has been significant. 

Indigenous species have been prioritized in nursery production. 

This has helped restore degraded lands and improve ecosystem services. 

The scheme also encourages the participation of youth. 

It promotes entrepreneurship in the field of forestry and horticulture. 

Workshops and training sessions are organized regularly. 

These sessions cover topics such as nursery management and sustainable practices. 

The government also collaborates with NGOs and local organizations. 

This collaboration enhances the reach and effectiveness of the scheme. 

Community involvement is a key aspect of the Decentralized People’s Nursery scheme. 

It fosters a sense of ownership among local populations. 

This leads to better conservation practices and sustainable management of resources. 

The scheme has also been instrumental in raising awareness about environmental issues. 

It encourages communities to take an active role in afforestation efforts. 

Overall, the Decentralized People’s Nursery scheme represents a significant step towards sustainable development. 

It combines economic benefits with ecological restoration. 

The scheme exemplifies the Government of India's commitment to environmental sustainability. 

It empowers local communities while addressing the pressing issue of deforestation. 

Through this initiative, the government aims to create a greener and more sustainable future for India.
